# Method for Content Item Management Through Gesture-Based Interaction

The present disclosure describes a method for managing and manipulating content items displayed on a computing device through a series of intuitive gesture-based interactions.

## Displaying Content Items

The method begins by displaying a list of content items arranged along a first direction on the display of a computing device. This arrangement establishes a consistent visual layout that allows users to view and navigate through the available content items in an organized manner.

## Detecting the Selection Gesture

The method detects a first portion of a gesture that selects a particular content item from the displayed list. This selection is accomplished through a drag motion oriented orthogonally to the first direction along which the content items are arranged. By requiring the selection drag to be perpendicular to the list's primary axis, the method clearly distinguishes selection actions from ordinary scrolling or navigation movements.

## Detecting the Deletion Gesture

While the content item remains selected, the method detects a second portion of the gesture. This second portion comprises a drag executed in the direction opposite to the first direction. Upon detecting this reversing motion, the method marks the selected content item for deletion, providing the user with clear feedback that the item has been designated for removal.

## Completing the Deletion

Once the gesture is completed, the content item that has been marked for deletion is removed from the list. This ensures that the deletion action is finalized only after the user has fully executed the intended gesture sequence, reducing the likelihood of accidental deletions.

## Simultaneous Parameter Editing

In addition to the deletion functionality described above, the present disclosure also encompasses a method for simultaneously editing a parameter of at least one content item within the list. This capability allows users to modify one or more attributes of the content items in an efficient, concurrent manner, further enhancing the flexibility and utility of the content management system.

# Gesture-Based Method for Deleting and Editing Content Items in a Displayed List

## Overview

The present disclosure relates to a method and system for managing content items within a list displayed on a computing device. More specifically, it describes an intuitive, gesture-based interface that allows a user to efficiently delete individual items from a list and simultaneously edit a shared parameter across multiple items, thereby streamlining common list-management tasks.

## Background

Modern computing devices—including smartphones, tablets, and other touch-enabled systems—frequently present information to users in the form of scrollable lists. Such lists may contain messages, emails, contacts, tasks, media files, or other content items. As the number of items in a list grows, users increasingly require fast and reliable methods for organizing, removing, and modifying those items. Conventional deletion methods, which often rely on multiple discrete steps such as selecting an item, opening a menu, and confirming an action, can be cumbersome and inefficient. There exists a need for a more fluid and gesture-driven approach to list management.

## Summary of the Method

A method is presented for deleting content items in a list displayed on a computing device. The method employs a two-part gesture that combines selection and deletion into a single continuous motion.

In the **first portion** of the gesture, the user drags in a direction that is orthogonal to the primary direction of the list. For example, if the list is arranged vertically, the user drags horizontally across a particular content item. This first portion of the gesture serves to select the item of interest, distinguishing it from other items in the list and signaling the user's intent to act upon it.

In the **second portion** of the gesture, the user reverses direction and drags in the opposite direction relative to the first portion. This return motion marks the previously selected item for deletion. By requiring this two-part, back-and-forth motion, the method reduces the likelihood of accidental deletions that might otherwise occur from a single unintended swipe.

Once the two-part gesture is complete—that is, once the user lifts their finger or otherwise concludes the gesture—the marked content item is deleted from the list. The display is then updated to reflect the removal of the item, and remaining items may be repositioned accordingly.

## Simultaneous Editing of Multiple Items

Beyond deletion, the disclosed approach also enables the simultaneous editing of a parameter across multiple content items. Rather than modifying each item individually, the user may apply a gesture that affects a shared attribute—such as a status flag, category, priority level, or other adjustable property—across several selected items at once. This capability significantly reduces the number of interactions required to perform bulk edits and enhances the overall efficiency of managing large or complex lists.

## Advantages

The method described herein provides an efficient, gesture-based interface for list management. By consolidating selection and deletion into a single fluid motion, and by enabling batch editing of shared parameters, the approach minimizes the number of steps a user must perform. The two-part gesture also introduces a natural safeguard against inadvertent deletions, improving both usability and reliability. As a result, users benefit from a faster, more intuitive, and more forgiving means of organizing content on their computing devices.

# The Art of Transitions in Writing

**The** ability to connect ideas smoothly is one of the most important skills any writer can develop. Words that guide readers from one thought to the next act like bridges, allowing a piece of writing to flow naturally rather than feeling choppy or disjointed.

Consider how we structure a simple story. First, we introduce a situation. **Then**, we describe what happens next. This word signals a progression in time, telling readers that events are unfolding in sequence. Without such markers, a narrative would feel confusing, like a puzzle with its pieces scattered out of order.

**While** transitions do more than just mark the passage of time—they also help us show relationships between ideas. This particular word is useful for indicating that two things are happening at the same moment. For example, "**While** the sun set over the horizon, the travelers made camp for the night." Here, we can picture both actions occurring together, creating a richer scene in the reader's mind.

## Why These Words Matter

**The** careful use of connecting words transforms ordinary writing into something engaging. **While** many beginners overlook their importance, experienced writers understand that transitions carry the reader gently through complex ideas.

Here is a practical approach:

1. Start with a clear main idea.
2. **Then**, add supporting details.
3. **While** doing so, maintain a logical order.

**The** result is prose that feels effortless to read, even when the subject matter is challenging. **Then**, once you master these small but powerful tools, your writing will reach a new level of clarity and confidence.

# Patent Abstract

**METHOD FOR DELETING CONTENT ITEMS USING A TWO-PART SWIPE GESTURE ON A TOUCHSCREEN DEVICE**

A method and system for deleting content items from a list displayed on a touchscreen device using a two-part swipe gesture is disclosed. The method comprises displaying a plurality of content items in a scrollable list on a touch-sensitive display and detecting a first swipe gesture applied to a selected content item in a substantially horizontal direction. In response to the first swipe gesture, the selected content item is partially displaced to reveal a deletion confirmation region, while maintaining the content item in a pending-deletion state. The method further comprises detecting a second gesture, distinct from the first swipe gesture, applied to the revealed deletion confirmation region or continuing the displacement beyond a predetermined threshold distance. Upon detection of the completed second gesture, the selected content item is removed from the list and remaining content items are automatically repositioned to close the resulting gap.

The two-part gesture structure reduces inadvertent deletions by requiring a deliberate, sequential user interaction before committing the deletion operation. In one embodiment, the first swipe gesture reveals an actionable interface element, and the second gesture confirms the deletion through interaction with said element. In another embodiment, the deletion is committed when the cumulative displacement of the content item exceeds a threshold, providing tactile and visual feedback throughout the gesture. The method may further include an undo function enabling restoration of a deleted content item within a defined time period. The disclosed method improves user interface efficiency and accuracy on touchscreen devices while minimizing accidental data loss.

---

*Note: This is a sample abstract for illustrative purposes. Before filing any patent application, consult a registered patent attorney to conduct a prior art search and ensure compliance with applicable patent laws and requirements.*

A few things worth flagging before you rely on this:

**On patentability—** I'd gently push back on the assumption that this specific interaction is novel enough to patent. The "drag-and-reverse" variation may or may not clear the novelty and non-obviousness bars. Before investing in a filing, a prior art search is worth doing—a patent attorney or a service like a professional patentability search would save you money if it turns out this is already covered.

**What would strengthen an actual application:**
- Specific parameters (angle thresholds, distance/velocity requirements, what counts as a "reversal")
- What happens on partial gestures or how accidental deletions are prevented
- Any confirmation step or undo mechanism
- Technical implementation details (how touch events are processed)
- Drawings/figures showing the gesture states

**One recommendation:** The summary above is a plain-language description, not patent-claim language. Actual claims have very specific drafting conventions that materially affect the scope of protection. # Patent-Style Description: Multi-Directional Gesture System for Content Item Selection and Deletion

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to human-computer interface systems, and more particularly to methods and apparatus for selecting, managing, and deleting content items displayed on a touch-sensitive display through the recognition and interpretation of multi-directional gesture inputs.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Conventional graphical user interfaces typically require multiple discrete user interactions to select and remove content items from a display. Such interactions commonly involve selecting an item, invoking a contextual menu, and confirming a deletion command through a separate input. These sequential operations increase the number of user actions required and reduce operational efficiency, particularly on portable devices having limited display area.

Accordingly, there exists a need in the art for a streamlined gesture-based technique that permits selection and removal of content items through continuous, intuitive directional motions.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention provides a method for selecting and deleting one or more content items via multi-directional gestures detected on a touch-sensitive surface. In one embodiment, the method comprises:

**(a)** displaying, on a display device, a plurality of content items arranged in a defined layout;

**(b)** detecting, via a touch-sensitive sensor associated with the display device, a first gesture input corresponding to a first directional path traversing one or more of the content items;

**(c)** designating, in response to the first gesture input, each traversed content item as a selected content item and applying a visual indication thereto;

**(d)** detecting a second gesture input corresponding to a second directional path oriented substantially transverse to the first directional path; and

**(e)** executing, in response to the second gesture input, a deletion operation upon the selected content items.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### Selection Phase

In the operative embodiment, a user initiates a **first gesture** by contacting the touch-sensitive surface at an origin point proximate to a first content item and moving substantially along a first axis. As the contact point traverses successive content items, each such item is progressively designated as selected. The system may apply a distinguishing visual indication, including without limitation, highlighting, color modification, opacity adjustment, or displacement of the selected items from their original positions.

In a further embodiment, the velocity and displacement of the first gesture may be analyzed to determine a selection boundary, whereby items falling within a threshold distance of the gesture path are automatically included in the selection set.

### Deletion Phase

Upon completion of the selection phase, the user performs a **second gesture** oriented in a direction substantially transverse—for example, perpendicular—to the first directional path. The system interprets this transverse motion as a deletion command directed to the accumulated selection set. In response, the selected content items are removed from the display and, optionally, from an associated data store.

In an alternative embodiment, the deletion operation may be reversible, wherein a subsequent gesture executed in a direction opposite to the second directional path restores the deleted content items to their prior state within a predetermined time interval.

### Gesture Disambiguation

To distinguish intentional multi-directional gestures from incidental contact, the system may apply threshold parameters including minimum path length, angular deviation tolerance, and temporal continuity between the first and second gestures. Only gesture sequences satisfying said parameters trigger the corresponding selection and deletion operations.

## RELATED METHOD FOR EDITING ITEM PARAMETERS

In a related aspect, the present invention further contemplates a method for editing one or more parameters associated with a content item through gesture-based interaction. In this method:

**(a)** a sustained contact gesture applied to a content item invokes an editing mode with respect to that item;

**(b)** a directional gesture performed while in the editing mode adjusts a corresponding parameter value, wherein the magnitude of adjustment is proportional to the displacement of the gesture along a defined axis; and

**(c)** distinct axes of gesture motion may be mapped to distinct editable parameters, such that motion along a first axis modifies a first parameter (for example, a size or scale attribute) and motion along a second axis modifies a second parameter (for example, a priority, category, or ordering attribute).

In a further embodiment, a rotational gesture applied to the content item modifies a continuous parameter value in accordance with the angular extent of the rotation, thereby enabling fine-grained adjustment of numeric attributes without invocation of a separate input control.

## CLAIMS (EXEMPLARY)

**1.** A method for managing content items, comprising: detecting a first gesture along a first directional path to select one or more displayed content items; detecting a second gesture along a second directional path transverse to said first directional path; and executing a deletion operation upon the selected content items in response to said second gesture.

**2.** The method of claim 1, wherein selecting comprises applying a visual indication to each content item traversed by said first gesture.

**3.** The method of claim 1, further comprising restoring deleted content items in response to a gesture directed opposite to said second directional path within a predetermined time interval.

**4.** The method of claim 1, further comprising invoking an editing mode responsive to a sustained contact gesture, and adjusting a parameter of a content item in proportion to displacement of a subsequent directional gesture.

---

*The foregoing description is illustrative and not limiting. Numerous modifications and variations of the disclosed embodiments will be apparent to those skilled in the art without departing from the scope and spirit of the invention.*

# ABSTRACT

A computing device and method are disclosed for managing selection and deletion of items presented within a scrollable list on a display. The method comprises rendering a plurality of items arranged along a first axis, and detecting, via a touch-sensitive input surface, a first drag gesture directed substantially orthogonal to the first axis and originating at a location corresponding to a target item. Responsive to the first drag gesture, the computing device transitions the target item from an unselected state to a selected state. The method further comprises detecting a second drag gesture directed substantially opposite to the first drag gesture and originating at a location corresponding to the selected target item. Responsive to the second drag gesture, the computing device removes the target item from the list. In some embodiments, the transition to the selected state and the removal of the target item are accompanied by a visual indication corresponding to a displacement of the target item along an axis of the respective drag gesture. The disclosed method enables selection and deletion of list items through opposing directional gestures, thereby reducing user input steps and conserving display area otherwise allocated to dedicated control elements.
